title: Burrito, beef, with beans and rice, cheese

content.title: About
content.content: A burrito with beef, beans, rice and cheese is a classic Mexican dish consisting of a large soft wheat tortilla filled with sautéed beef, cooked beans, fluffy rice and melted cheese. The dish is popular worldwide for its rich flavor, convenience and the ability to customize the fillings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Burritos originated in northern Mexico where wheat flour was more available than corn.
Traditional beef is seasoned with cumin, paprika, chili and garlic, giving it a distinctive aroma.
Black or pinto beans are commonly used, providing protein and fiber.
Mexican‑style rice is often cooked with tomato paste and turmeric, giving it a golden hue.
Cheese such as cheddar or Mexican “queso” melts smoothly and binds the other ingredients.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Beef and beans supply complete amino acids, supporting muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Beans and rice provide dietary fiber that promotes digestive health and helps regulate blood sugar.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Beef offers heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Contains calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Cheese adds calcium and a modest amount of vitamin D, supporting bone health.

items.title: Sustained energy
items.content: Carbohydrates from rice and fats from cheese give lasting satiety and fuel for active days.

items.title: High saturated fat
items.content: Cheese and certain cuts of beef can be high in saturated fat, so people with heart disease should watch portion size.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Seasonings and cheese add salt, which may be a concern for those with hypertension.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese can trigger reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Portion control
items.content: Burritos are calorie‑dense; overconsumption may lead to weight gain if eaten frequently.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Burritos are hand‑held, but they can also be sliced in half and served with salsa, guacamole or sour cream. For a lighter version, substitute part of the beef with turkey or add extra vegetables such as tomatoes, avocado or lettuce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store a prepared burrito in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. For freezing, wrap tightly in plastic film and place in a freezer bag – it keeps well for up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly to ensure the filling is evenly hot.
